_README: FIXTURE 4 (seeds half) — THE ADVERSARIAL EDGE CASES. MUST PASS, every one.
This fixture is the one that keeps the lint USABLE. Fixtures 1 and 2 prove it catches
what it should; this one proves it does NOT catch what it shouldn't. A lint that cries
wolf gets disabled by the team within a week, and a disabled lint protects nothing —
so a false positive here is exactly as serious as a miss in fixture 1.
Every entry below is multi-word and/or contains an entity name, so a naive
'ban compound concatenations' rule flags most of them. Each must pass, for a reason:

seeds._why_it_must_pass: A Latin binomial is ONE name. The ontology deliberately lists both 'bacopa monnieri' and the bare genus 'bacopa', so BOTH match — a naive two-forms-of-one-entity rule flags it. Their token spans OVERLAP ([0,2) vs [0,1)), so it is one name, not a juxtaposition. This is the span-overlap predicate earning its keep.

THE SHARPEST TRAP IN THE CORPUS. 'kapikacchu mucuna' MUST FAIL (Rule A) while 'mucuna pruriens' MUST PASS — and 'mucuna' is a synonym appearing in both. The binomial's span subsumes the bare synonym's, so only the genuine juxtaposition fires. Same entity, opposite verdicts, one predicate.
The parent alone is the REAL head term: 301,000 US. Banning 'turmeric curcumin' must not ban 'turmeric'.

The constituent ALONE is a legitimate entity and a legitimate query in its own right: 60,500 US at CPC $2.48 (2.9x turmeric's $0.86 — a commercially distinct supplement-buyer query). Rule B bans the WELD, never either half. The old artifact destroyed this distinction and lost both numbers.
A synonym on its own is just a name. Only the juxtaposition of two names for one referent is banned.

The OTHER name for the same entity, alone, is also just a name. Rule A bans 'tulsi holy basil' — it must not ban either term separately. Both are tested SEPARATELY; that is the corollary rule, not a loophole.

A real modifier query, 201,000 US. 'benefits' names no entity, so no two forms of one entity are juxtaposed. Ahrefs' seed method #1 — variations OF A REAL TERM ALREADY IN HAND — is legitimate and this is it.

THE COMMISSION'S NAMED CASE. A legitimate long-tail phrase, verbatim from the audience corpus. Four words, no entity juxtaposition. If the lint flags this, the lint is wrong and the whole gate loses its credibility.

seeds.seed: is ashwagandha safe with blood pressure medication
seeds.source_quote: is ashwagandha safe with blood pressure medication
seeds._why_it_must_pass: A long, natural, high-intent YMYL question in the audience's own register. Contains exactly one entity name. Length is not a signal of invention — PROVENANCE is.
Hinglish, verbatim from the corpus. 33,100/mo — MORE than Devanagari अश्वगंधा at 22,200. The register IS the keyword; 'ke fayde' is not noise to be normalised away into 'benefits of'.
Devanagari must survive tokenisation intact. A tokeniser that drops non-ASCII makes every Hindi seed invisible to the lint — failure #3 wearing a different hat.
A question-shaped seed containing no ontology entity at all. Must pass on provenance alone.
